title: Accents and the h
tagline: What each accent does, words told apart by an accent, and the aspirated h.
goal: Know what each French accent shows, tell a / à, ou / où or la / là apart, and recognise words with an aspirated h, which block elision and liaison.

blocks.text: French accents are not decoration and not stress marks: they change **the sound** of a vowel or tell two words apart. Leaving them out is a spelling mistake.

head: Accent
What it does
Examples
rows: closed e, like «ay» without the y
open e; often marks a lost s
c sounds like s before a, o, u

blocks.title: The circumflex hides an s
blocks.text: When you see *â, ê, î, ô, û*, try adding an s: *hôpital* → hospital, *île* → isle, *fête* → feast, *côte* → coast, *bête* → beast, *forêt* → forest.
Review the sound of each vowel in [[1]].
Sometimes the accent is the only thing that separates two words:

items.tr: He has a house in Paris.
Tea or coffee? — Where's the coffee?

blocks.text: Capitals keep their accents too: *À bientôt, École*. The keyboard in the app has buttons for all of them.
The French h is **never pronounced** (*hôtel* = «otel»). But there are two kinds, and you can tell by the words around them:

The most common ones with an aspirated h: *le hasard* (chance), *le haricot* (bean), *la honte* (shame), *le héros*, *le hibou* (owl), *le homard* (lobster), *le hamburger*, *le hockey*, *en haut* (upstairs), *le huit*.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.text: With a liaison, *les‿héros* would sound like «les zéros» (the zeros). So: *les │ héros*.

checklist: I know French accents change the sound, not the stress.
I tell *é, è, ê* apart and use the *ç*.
I don't mix up *a / à, ou / où, la / là, sur / sûr*.
I recognise words with an aspirated h: no elision, no liaison.

challenge.title: Circumflex hunt
challenge.text: Find ten words with *â, ê, î, ô* or *û* in a French text (a news article, a song) and try to guess the hidden English word by adding an s. How many did you get?
